scope: Selected scientific construction, caption/figure interpretation and custody clauses in the 27 assigned sequencing-basics support paths, with complete eligible associated context. This is not a new full ordinary-lesson denominator.

rows.requirement: Total region copy count and distinguishable sequence versions are separate quantities.
A and B are arbitrary inherited-version placeholders, not functional, parental or healthy/damaged labels.
The fictional 1+1 state retains two versions in two total copies.
The fictional 2+0 state has two total copies and one retained original version: copy-neutral LOH.
The fictional 1+0 state has one copy with version loss under the stated model.
The fictional 2+1 state has three copies with both versions retained.
Major/minor counts rank estimated allelic contributions; minor zero supports modeled LOH and does not establish parental identity or phase.
Allele-aware copy inference combines relative coverage and informative allelic balance with purity/ploidy context.
Matched-normal information and heterozygous informative positions help distinguish version retention; a total-copy profile alone cannot separate 1+1 from 2+0.
Bulk fitted segments can reflect mixture and subclonality rather than the same count in every cell.
Copy loss/gain alone establishes neither retained sequence function nor expression, dependency or treatment benefit.
The copy-neutral exercise retains two copies and leaves function to separate sequence/expression/functional evidence.
HLA typing, sampled-tumor allele-specific DNA retention and current peptide display are distinct evidence questions.
The three mechanism panels distinguish allele-specific DNA loss, reduced expression and impaired B2M support.
Loss of one allele or linked haplotype does not mean that every class-I allele has been lost.
A DNA call is not a measurement of current surface-display amount or function; dashed figure links are qualified accordingly.
A1 and A2 are placeholders rather than named HLA alleles, measured surface counts or real patient findings.
HLA variability, patient-specific sequences, informative matched-normal evidence and purity/ploidy affect allele-aware inference.
Normal admixture, mixed tumor populations and sampled regions limit what a weak or regional loss call can establish.
A proposed target dependent on a lost presenting allele is challenged without proving failure of all vaccine targets or a successful alternative treatment.
B2M supports classical class-I assembly across multiple alleles, a different mechanism from an allele-specific HLA DNA loss.
A connected long molecule can link separated sequence features and support phasing under an appropriate method.
Long sequence reads and chemical-mark evidence are separate capabilities; one does not establish that the other was measured.
Native-DNA nanopore modification inference needs retained signal and a supported trained model, not sequence letters alone.
SMRT modification inference uses polymerase timing/kinetic information and an appropriate model rather than read length alone.
Ordinary amplification of unconverted DNA copies sequence without faithfully copying original methylation marks into its products; it does not erase the original molecule physically.
Conversion before amplification is a distinct workflow that can encode chemical-state information for later sequence reading.
Eight marked calls among ten usable molecules at one site is a fictional 80 percent molecule fraction.
That site-specific molecule fraction is not automatically a malignant-cell fraction or fraction of genes silenced.
A modification-call probability for one molecule differs from a fraction across measured molecules.
Molecule integrity, preparation, retained signals, supported modification classes and controls belong with the claimed capability.
Chemical marks and connected sequence do not alone establish expression, cellular origin or treatment benefit.
Depth counts usable observations at a position under stated read/base/alignment/overlap/duplicate filters.
Mean depth averages positions; coverage breadth uses a named target-base denominator and an explicit usable-depth criterion.
Read depth is separate from independently represented molecular depth.
The fictional report stipulates mean 100x, local 4x, and 900/1000 target bases reaching illustrative 20x, giving 90 percent breadth.
In the native drawing the 100x and 4x bars share a zero and scale, with the illustrative 20x line between them.
No full per-base vector is supplied, so the stated mean cannot be independently recomputed from the figure.
The 20x reporting criterion is fictional and does not establish a diagnostic cutoff or variant-detection limit.
More sequencing cannot create new original molecules from duplicates or recover territory absent from a prepared library.
Library complexity, recovery, capture, preservation and alignment can change the usable evidence.
Variant sensitivity must be validated end to end for the intended specimen, region, alteration class and pipeline.
An adequate mean/breadth summary does not establish usable evidence or a reliable negative at every important position.
Four drawn usable read observations at one position do not prove four independent source molecules.
Five paired-end pairs contain ten reads but at most five represented library fragments before duplicate/ancestry interpretation.
A separate fictional one-source/three-copy/six-read vignette is not added to the five-pair example.
A read, an alignment record, a library fragment and an independently represented source molecule are different counting units.
Coordinate duplicate rules depend on preparation; shared primer-defined endpoints in an amplicon assay do not establish common ancestry alone.
Molecular tags and duplicate recognition do not automatically repair errors introduced before tagging.
Phred Q20 and Q30 express model-estimated per-base error probabilities of 1 percent and 0.1 percent, not mutation-truth probabilities.
Confident base identification and confident alignment location are separate questions.
Library preparation, instrument signal, base calling, quality and alignment precede usable question-specific sequence evidence.
A read count alone establishes neither cells, somatic origin, function nor clinical benefit.
Panels, exomes and genomes label intended DNA territory; exact target coordinates and analyzed change classes remain assay specific.
A targeted panel can include selected non-exon regions, not only named coding genes.
An exome primarily targets exons; exons include retained untranslated sequence and capture designs vary.
Broad genome coverage includes coding and noncoding territory but can leave difficult repeat regions or positions poorly measured.
Blank positions outside the toy design and hatched potential gaps inside intended targets have separate meanings.
Four invented aligned reads overlap P and two overlap Q; R is inside the toy target with zero usable reads.
Territory and average depth do not rank local sensitivity or prove complete variant detection.
Each claimed alteration class needs the intended workflow and validation rather than inference from the territory label.
Conventional DNA genome sequencing does not automatically establish RNA/protein/function or methylation measurement.
A negative substitution result cannot exclude an untested fusion breakpoint or unsupported alteration class.
The same-interval track widths, exon positions and gaps are schematic rather than genomic coordinates, measured depth or fixed category performance.
Both idealized mixtures contain 50 cancer and 50 diploid normal cells, so cell purity stays 50 percent and CCF stays 100 percent.
With two local cancer copies and one variant copy in every cancer cell, 50 variant copies among 200 total predict 25 percent VAF.
With one remaining local variant copy per cancer cell, 50 among 150 predict about 33 percent VAF without changing cell mixture or CCF.
Local copy number and global ploidy are different denominators; local-copy bars do not describe gene activity or whole-genome ploidy.
The expected fraction assumes uniform copy state, fixed variant multiplicity, diploid normal cells and unbiased recovery/sequencing.
Observed VAF counts usable reads or assay-defined molecules; CCF is a model-dependent cancer-cell proportion.
The simple mixture relation uses p*f*m divided by p*C+2*(1-p), with model uncertainty and richer subclonal copy states kept separate.
High or changing VAF alone establishes neither cellular origin/function nor shared truncal ancestry across lesions.
The two panels are simultaneous hypothetical alternatives rather than a measured time course or cell census.
Cell purity, DNA contribution and pathology tumor-bed area are different quantities and cannot be silently substituted.
Twenty-four mutation tokens are a fictional count inventory, not specified genomic locations or proof of identical variants across workflows.
Twenty-four eligible mutations across 2 Mb give the simplified density 12 mut/Mb.
Twenty-four eligible mutations across 1 Mb give the simplified density 24 mut/Mb; one megabase is one million DNA bases.
Mutation classes, inherited-variant/artifact filtering and any calibration belong with numerator and denominator.
Eligible territory is assay specific; equal units do not make panels and exomes clinically interchangeable.
Mutation density does not directly measure protein production, peptide presentation, immune recognition or treatment benefit.
Research arithmetic does not itself satisfy a clinical authorized-test, specimen or disease-setting requirement.
The bounded pembrolizumab TMB-high example must preserve the label date, authorized test, disease/prior-treatment/alternative requirements and accelerated-approval/pediatric-CNS limitations.
The native 2 Mb and 1 Mb ribbons share an intended relative scale without encoding measured genomes or a response cutoff.
The Friends harmonization comparison is computational assay-method evidence rather than a treatment-selection equivalence trial.
